mfg1-surface-lesson-061.title: Explain surface changes and finish types in polishing
mfg1-surface-lesson-061.objective:
Separate material removal from gloss finishing.
Distinguish mirror, satin and hairline requirements.
mfg1-surface-lesson-061.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on surface changes, 8 on three finishes and 7 organizing the line-direction example. Write the difference between grit and roughness in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-061.summary:
Check lines, roughness and dimensions as well as gloss.
Treat grit numbers and actual roughness separately.
safety: Avoid damaging dimensions or edges through excessive polishing.
Do not change rotational conditions without authorization to alter the finish target.

paragraphs.title: Consider how unevenness changes
paragraphs.text: Polishing moves from removing coarse scratches and projections toward finer finishes. The aim is lower surface roughness as processing progresses, but later steps do not remove every scratch. Check prior-process quality and removal amount.

paragraphs.title: More gloss is not always better
paragraphs.text: Mirror finishing aims for mirror-like gloss. Satin uses fine short lines and hairline uses aligned fine lines to reduce gloss. Do not accept products with different requirements merely because they are the shiniest.

paragraphs.title: Do not confuse grit numbers with roughness
paragraphs.text: Grit numbers indicate abrasive fineness, but results vary with product systems, material and condition. Grit number and measured surface roughness are different quantities. Compare the specified buff and compound, preceding and following processes and measurement conditions.

paragraphs.title: Check line direction too
paragraphs.text: If a hairline-specified part develops near-mirror gloss, few scratches alone do not establish acceptance. Check specified line direction, appearance sample and inspection conditions. Identify affected items and request a decision.

terms.meaning: A characteristic expressing fine surface unevenness.
A finish that reduces gloss using fine lines and similar effects.
A finish creating aligned fine lines.
A numbering system indicating abrasive fineness.

mfg1-surface-lesson-062.title: Separate polishing dwell marks from edge-coating peeling
mfg1-surface-lesson-062.objective:
Separately observe scratches, insufficient gloss and concentrated polishing.
Consider edge-pressure concentration and holding.
mfg1-surface-lesson-062.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 classifying defects, 8 on dwell and edges and 7 organizing recurrence information. Write the problems with unauthorized rework in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-062.summary:
Separate heat, scratches, concentrated polishing and edge peeling.
Preserve positions and conditions to support approved measures.
safety: Do not inspect, replace or clean a buff while it is running.
Do not hide peeling with unauthorized polishing; identify it and follow the required decision process.

paragraphs.title: Describe appearance defects specifically
paragraphs.text: Record burn as heat discoloration, unevenness as a nonuniform finish, and scratches as linear damage. For insufficient gloss, compare the buff, compound and preceding process. Pressing harder without investigating can create further heat or shape defects.

paragraphs.title: Processing concentrates in one place
paragraphs.text: Continuous polishing at the same location can produce depressions, unevenness and burns. Check holding, feed, pressure and buff wear. Do not confuse the defect name buff dwell mark with electrical power being switched off.

paragraphs.title: Edge peeling and rounding
paragraphs.text: Pressure concentrated at corners or edges can round corners or peel coatings from plated items. Check holding, contact angle, force and required coating thickness. Merely polishing away visible evidence is different from restoring quality.

paragraphs.title: Preserve recurrence information
paragraphs.text: For repeated edge peeling, compile location diagrams, adjacent processes, tool operating time and holding method. Do not assume an operator's increased speed solved it. The responsible person evaluates the issue, and quality is checked under the same conditions after approved measures.

terms.meaning: A condition with less gloss than required.
Linear surface damage.
A defect name used here for polishing concentrated at one location.
A defect in which coating peels at an edge or similar location.

mfg1-surface-lesson-063.title: Organize thickness-measurement principles and effects on samples
mfg1-surface-lesson-063.objective:
Separate light, magnetic, electromagnetic, cross-section and mass methods.
Do not equate nondestructive with hazard-free or universally applicable.
mfg1-surface-lesson-063.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on three non-sectioning methods, 8 on sections and mass and 7 making a method comparison. Explain nondestructive versus safe in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-063.summary:
Match principle, substrate/coating compatibility, location and calibration.
Nondestructive classification does not permit omitting safety controls.
safety: X-ray instruments and chemical coating removal require specified training and authority.
Do not cut or dissolve shipping products for measurement without authorization.

paragraphs.title: What is detected and converted to thickness?
paragraphs.text: X-ray fluorescence evaluates element-related X-rays; magnetic and eddy-current methods use electromagnetic properties of substrate and coating. Applicability varies with material, layer structure, shape and surface condition. A method name alone does not establish suitability for every metal coating.

paragraphs.title: Cross-section and mass-difference methods
paragraphs.text: Microscopic cross-section methods prepare and observe a section. Coating-mass methods evaluate the mass difference before and after removal, among other approaches. Conversion to thickness requires checks of area, density and removal conditions. Distinguish measurement locations and the extent of averaging.

paragraphs.title: Nondestructive does not mean hazard-free
paragraphs.text: Methods evaluating without cutting or dissolving the sample are called nondestructive, but X-ray and other instruments need dedicated controls. Destructive/nondestructive classification alone does not determine operating authority or human safety. Check reference plates, suitable reference samples and calibration too.

paragraphs.title: Ask when changing methods
paragraphs.text: Two instruments displaying μm may differ in principle and applicability. If old and new methods disagree, do not select only the favorable result. Align samples, positions, calibration, substrates and coatings, and report to the responsible person.

terms.reading: けいこうえっくすせん
terms.meaning: Element-related X-rays generated when matter is irradiated with X-rays.
Circulating current induced electromagnetically inside a conductor.
The difference between two masses, such as before and after treatment.
A suitable sample used as a reference for measurement checks.

mfg1-surface-lesson-064.title: Record design, manufacturing and logistics quality separately
mfg1-surface-lesson-064.objective:
Distinguish customer requirements from manufacturing convenience.
Check the supply process as well as product performance.
mfg1-surface-lesson-064.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on quality requirements, 8 on three stages and 7 organizing a shipping example. Check handover information in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-064.summary:
Connect design, manufacturing and logistics through requirements.
Do not define quality solely by manufacturing convenience.
safety: Do not omit packing or transport safety procedures to meet delivery dates.
Do not change customer specifications or inspection plans without authorization.

paragraphs.title: Consider quality as meeting requirements
paragraphs.text: Quality concerns how well customer or user expectations and requirements are met. Ease, speed or good appearance is insufficient by itself. Check reliability, safety, necessary performance and intended use. Do not change to high gloss or thick coating while requirements are unclear.

paragraphs.title: Separate three stages
paragraphs.text: Design quality concerns the intended quality, manufacturing quality realizing the designed performance consistently, and logistics quality the journey to the customer: correct items, quantity, delivery time and transport condition. An inspection-passed item scratched during packing may no longer meet requirements.

paragraphs.title: Pass information onward
paragraphs.text: When changes occur, connect requirements, drawing editions, processes, inspection and packing conditions. The workplace must not independently reduce inspection items or substitute cheaper materials. Investigate differences using receipt, in-process, storage and shipping records, not only final checks.

paragraphs.title: Match quantity and condition
paragraphs.text: Even a lot with acceptable thickness has a quality problem if specified quantities are missing or transport scratches appear. Record manufacturing results separately from packing and shipping history, and report causes and responses to the responsible person.

terms.meaning: Quality targeted during planning and design.
Quality realizing the design intent in the product.
Quality of items, quantities, delivery and condition until arrival at the customer.
Performance or conditions needed by the customer.

mfg1-surface-lesson-065.title: Distinguish water-quality indicators and air impacts
mfg1-surface-lesson-065.objective:
Explain differences among pH, metals, COD, BOD and SS.
Separate source assessment from surrounding-environment assessment.
mfg1-surface-lesson-065.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on five water indicators, 8 on treatment and air and 7 preparing an abnormality report. Distinguish the targets of criteria in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-065.summary:
Water indicators concern different targets.
Record and check equipment emissions and surrounding conditions separately.
safety: Do not mix unknown waste liquids to test treatment effectiveness.
Do not approach gases or leaks to smell or touch them.

paragraphs.title: One number does not describe all water quality
paragraphs.text: pH concerns acidity and alkalinity, metal concentration the amount of a target metal, and SS suspended solids. COD and BOD evaluate water quality as chemical and biochemical oxygen demand respectively. Transparency or pH alone cannot reveal all these indicators.

paragraphs.title: Combine treatment methods
paragraphs.text: Wastewater methods include physical separation, chemical and biological treatment, combined according to purpose and composition. Systems containing cyanide, chromium and similar substances require dedicated management. Representative textbook names do not determine neutralizers or mixing order; follow trained personnel's procedures.

paragraphs.title: Airborne substances and their effects
paragraphs.text: Smoke, dust and volatile organic compounds have different sources. SOx and NOx relate to acid rain and other effects; VOC and NOx also participate in photochemical reactions. Do not confuse environmental-condition criteria with equipment-emission criteria. Check the current applicable conditions.

paragraphs.title: Communicate abnormalities
paragraphs.text: For changed exhaust flow, unusual smells, leaks or neighborhood complaints, organize time, location, equipment and operating conditions. Reduced smell alone does not establish safety; obtain necessary inspection and measurement.

terms.meaning: Chemical oxygen demand, a water-quality indicator.
Biochemical oxygen demand, a water-quality indicator.
An indicator associated with suspended solids in water.
An abbreviation for volatile organic compounds.

mfg1-surface-lesson-066.title: Read scales and menisci according to conditions
mfg1-surface-lesson-066.objective:
Check each division and the minimum unit.
Distinguish reading positions for different instruments.
mfg1-surface-lesson-066.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 calculating divisions, 8 on three instruments and 7 calculating the difference example. Check recording conditions in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-066.summary:
First check unit, division value and reading position.
Keep instrument conditions and initial and final readings.
safety: Do not move too close to chemicals or live parts to read a scale.
Clean and sample with designated protective equipment and procedures.

paragraphs.title: Count intervals between numbers
paragraphs.text: For analog instruments, check units and range, then divide the difference between two numbered points by the number of intervals to obtain one division. Do not confuse line counts and interval counts. Viewing angle and pointer thickness also matter, so follow the specified reading method.

paragraphs.title: Read the surface appropriate to the instrument
paragraphs.text: The curved liquid surface is called a meniscus. Burettes, pipettes and hydrometers may specify different positions, such as the upper or lower edge. Do not transfer one textbook instrument example to every instrument; check the instrument and measurement-method specifications.

paragraphs.title: Keep both readings when using a difference
paragraphs.text: Volume used from a burette is the difference between initial and final readings. Check scale direction and units; the final reading alone is not the used volume. Also check temperature, bubbles, contact and leaks that can disturb measurement.

paragraphs.title: Practice with different numbers
paragraphs.text: In a paper burette example, initial 2.6 mL and final 17.4 mL give 14.8 mL used. Check reading and subtraction separately. Do not round actual measurements into tidier numbers that differ from the observed values.

terms.meaning: The amount represented between adjacent scale marks.
The curved liquid surface inside a container.
A reading change caused by a shifted viewing position.
Determining a quantity from a display or scale.

mfg1-surface-lesson-067.title: Separate analytical objectives from deposition phenomena
mfg1-surface-lesson-067.objective:
Read the purposes of neutralization, redox and chelate analysis.
Do not combine precipitation and electrode deposition into one phenomenon.
mfg1-surface-lesson-067.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on analytical targets, 8 on three solid-forming phenomena and 7 reading an acid-concentration sheet. Write necessary inquiries in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-067.summary:
Match analysis methods to target constituents.
A visible solid alone does not identify composition or reaction.
safety: Do not add reagents to actual liquids to try textbook reactions.
Do not confuse analysis with decisions to replenish or discard actual tank liquids.

paragraphs.title: What is measured, and how much?
paragraphs.text: Quantitative analysis determines the amount of a target constituent. Neutralization titration, redox analysis, chelate analysis and separating a precipitate to measure it use different reactions and targets. Even with the same metal name, a method may measure another constituent or acidity.

paragraphs.title: Consider how a solid appears
paragraphs.text: Precipitation of a sparingly soluble solid in solution, deposition by reducing metal ions at an electrode, and solid separation by cooling or evaporation have different conditions despite all producing solids. The broad word deposition alone does not identify the reaction or composition.

paragraphs.title: Record reaction and measurement conditions
paragraphs.text: On an analysis sheet, check sample name, target, sampled amount, concentration units, method and pretreatment. Acidity results do not prove all metal constituents are suitable. Before comparing methods, check whether they target the same quantity.

paragraphs.title: Prevent target confusion
paragraphs.text: If a bath result lists only acid concentration, do not treat metal concentration as already measured. Compare required control items and methods with the responsible person. Do not independently add another reagent to identify a precipitate.

terms.meaning: Analysis determining the amount of a target constituent.
Analysis using complex formation with metals and related effects.
A property of being difficult to dissolve under specified conditions.
A solid separating and appearing from solution or a similar medium.
